To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distal enhancer and the proximal enhancer are both required for the induction of AFP gene expression during liver injury, that the proximal enhancers is required for the induction, but not maintenance, of AFP gene expression in the liver, and that the proximal and distal sequences are both required for appropriate spatial regulation of the transgenes in the liver.

The AFP gene is regulated by at least three enhancers, a repressor element, and a proximal promoter; the distal enhancers are required for liver regeneration; the proximal promoter is necessary for liver regeneration, but not for the developmental regulation; and, the repressor element is required for postnatal repression, but not for liver regeneration

two DNA sequences are required to induce the expression of an AFP transgene in the mouse liver during regeneration and that the expression of the transgene is first found in all liver cells and then is localized to the perinecrotized hepatocytes surrounding the centrilobular vein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular regulation of the alpha-fetoprotien (AFP) gene during liver regeneration.
understanding the mechanisms of liver regeneration and the role that the liver plays in development.
the regulation of alpha-fetoproteins (AFP) during liver development and liver regeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a proximal sequence is required for the regulation of the AFP gene during liver regeneration.
a combination of distal and proximal sequences is necessary and sufficient for the induction of AFP gene expression during liver injury.
a distal enhancer and a proximal enhancer are necessary and sufficient for the regulation of AFP gene transcription during liver regeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the distal sequence is sufficient to direct the appropriate tissue-specific expression of AFP in transgenic mice and the proximal sequence is required to direct the appropriate developmental regulation of the gene.

AFP gene expression during liver development and liver regeneration is regulated by a complex network of regulatory sequences, and that the proximal promoter, a distal enhancer, and a postnatal repressor are required for the appropriate regulation of AFP gene activity in response to liver injury
the proximal promoter and a region between 118 bp upstream and 838 bp downstream of the transcriptional start site are required for AFP gene induction after liver injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AFP gene is regulated by two distinct enhancer sequences, one proximal and one distal.
a distal enhancer and proximal promoter are sufficient to direct liver regeneration-specific gene expression in vivo.

a combination of two DNA sequences, one located distal to the structural gene and the other proximal to the transcriptional start site, is necessary and sufficient for the induction of AFP gene expression in response to liver damage.
